chapter_theme: The one song at Srisailam (திருமலை): the poet asks to know the constituents of the self, reach the feet within, and see the six-faced Lord, rather than wander the streets in idle talk.

523.reading: The poet asks that, knowing the ten, twenty, sixty and six, he seek the two feet within, melt, and shine with the light of the full moon and fire in inner space, and that he not wander in the streets talking with everyone like a block of wood, but be granted the sight of the six-faced Lord. The praise names Ganapati of the great belly, who eats fruit, gram, pulses and sweets and wrote the ancient tale, as Murugan's elder brother, and Tirumalai where elephants and deer roam.
523.nuance: ஒருபது இருபது அறுபது உடன் அறு adds to ninety-six, the number of tattvas in the Tamil Siddha count; that reading is mine, and the song does not name them. தெருவினில் மரமென, like a tree in the street, sets idle talk against inward seeing. பழமொழி எழுதிய கணபதி is Ganapati as scribe of the Bharata.
